objects.description: Scoped enumeration of all lexical token kinds recognized by the reshadefx tokenizer, including operators, identifiers, literals, keywords, preprocessor directives, and comments.
Represents a single lexical token with its kind, source location, span, and literal value in multiple representations. Provides conversion to tokenid and a helper to stringify token IDs.

reshadefx::lexer is a C-like language lexical analyzer that tokenizes an input string. It maintains current input position and location, with options to ignore comments, whitespace, preprocessor and line directives, and keywords, and to escape string literals. It provides methods to lex the next token, skip whitespace or to the next line, and reset position. Construction requires an input string and optional behavior flags. Destruction is trivial; no external resource ownership beyond internal strings and pointers. Note: types 'location' and 'token' are referenced from effect_token.hpp and are not defined here.

Parsed value type descriptor used by the reshadefx compiler. Encodes base datatype, vector/matrix dimensions, qualifiers, array length, and associated struct id. Provides helpers for type merging, ranking for overload resolution, description, and various predicates.

functions.signature: reshadefx::lexer::lexer(std::string input, bool ignore_comments = true, bool ignore_whitespace = true, bool ignore_pp_directives = true, bool ignore_line_directives = false, bool ignore_keywords = false, bool escape_string_literals = true, const reshadefx::location &start_location = reshadefx::location())
functions.description: Constructs a lexical analyzer for C-like languages over the provided input string. The boolean flags configure whether comments, whitespace, preprocessor directives, line directives, and keywords are ignored during tokenization, and whether string literals are escaped. The optional start_location sets the initial source position metadata. Typical usage: create a lexer with desired options, then call lex()/skip_* as you iterate tokens.
requirements: The input parameter provides the entire source text to be lexed.
The start_location should represent a valid initial source position for the input (e.g., beginning of file); exact semantics beyond being a location object are not specified.
Behavior of tokenization is affected by the boolean flags; callers should set them consistently before tokenization begins.

functions.name: reshadefx::lexer::operator=
functions.description: Assigns this lexer from another, copying the input, current position (offset and end), and all configuration flags. After assignment, this lexer will continue lexing the same input from the same position as the source at the time of assignment.
requirements: The source lexer must be a valid, initialized reshadefx::lexer instance.
After assignment, previously held input and position of the destination lexer are replaced.

functions.name: reshadefx::lexer::input_offset
functions.description: Returns the current position in the input string as a character offset from the start. Useful for saving/restoring positions or for diagnostics.
requirements: Meaningful only relative to the current input_string() associated with this lexer.

functions.name: reshadefx::lexer::input_string
functions.description: Provides a const reference to the entire input string being lexed. Use this to inspect the original source or to compute bounds for offsets.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the lexer object remains alive.
The caller must not attempt to modify the returned string (it is const).

functions.name: reshadefx::lexer::lex
functions.description: Performs lexical analysis and returns the next token from the input, advancing the current position. Behavior respects the configured ignore_* and escape_string_literals options.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed lexer.
Return/token kinds and end-of-input behavior are defined by reshadefx::token; specific error tokens or exceptions are unknown from this header.

functions.name: reshadefx::lexer::skip_space

requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed lexer.

functions.name: reshadefx::lexer::skip_to_next_line
functions.description: Advances the current position to the start of the next line, ignoring intervening tokens.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed lexer.

functions.name: reshadefx::lexer::reset_to_offset

The caller should ensure offset corresponds to a valid character boundary within the input (the input is a std::string; encoding-specific considerations are up to the caller).

Should be paired with prior enter_namespace calls to maintain proper namespace stack balance.

functions.name: reshadefx::symbol_table::current_scope
functions.description: Return a const reference to the current scope in which the symbol table operates. Useful for qualified lookups or for passing scope context to other operations.
requirements: No explicit preconditions documented.
Returned reference remains valid as long as the symbol_table object remains alive and scopes are managed internally.

functions.name: reshadefx::symbol_table::insert_symbol
functions.signature: bool reshadefx::symbol_table::insert_symbol(const std::string &name, const reshadefx::symbol &symbol, bool global = false);
functions.description: Insert a new symbol under the given name into the symbol table. Returns false if a symbol with the same name and type already exists. The optional 'global' flag indicates insertion at global scope rather than the current scope.
requirements: No explicit preconditions documented for name contents.
The provided symbol object should be initialized appropriately for its symbol_type; specifics not documented.
Return value must be checked: false indicates an existing conflicting symbol (same name and type).
Behavior and exact meaning of the 'global' flag are inferred from its name and default value; no further guarantees documented.

functions.name: reshadefx::symbol_table::find_symbol
functions.description: Look up an existing symbol by name, searching according to the table’s scoping rules, and return the symbol data together with the scope in which it was found.
requirements: No explicit preconditions documented for the name argument.
Returned symbol may be invalid (e.g., op == symbol_type::invalid) if not found; exact not-found semantics are not documented in this header.

functions.name: reshadefx::symbol_table::find_symbol
functions.signature: reshadefx::scoped_symbol reshadefx::symbol_table::find_symbol(const std::string &name, const reshadefx::scope &scope, bool exclusive) const;
functions.description: Look up an existing symbol by name starting from a specified scope. If 'exclusive' is true, the search likely only considers that scope; otherwise it may consider parent scopes as well. Returns the symbol together with the scope where it was found.
requirements: The scope argument should be a scope object obtained from this symbol_table (inferred; not explicitly documented).
Semantics of the 'exclusive' flag are inferred from its name; exact behavior is not documented.
No explicit preconditions documented for the name argument.
Returned symbol’s not-found semantics are not documented in this header.

functions.name: reshadefx::symbol_table::resolve_function_call
functions.signature: bool reshadefx::symbol_table::resolve_function_call(const std::string &name, const std::vector<reshadefx::expression> &args, const reshadefx::scope &scope, reshadefx::symbol &data, bool &ambiguous) const;
functions.description: Search for the best matching function or intrinsic overload with the given name and argument list, considering the provided scope, and return its symbol data. Sets 'ambiguous' when multiple equally good matches exist. Returns true on successful resolution.
requirements: The args vector should contain valid expression objects compatible with the effect system; exact requirements are not documented here.
The scope should represent the context in which to resolve the call; origin requirements are not documented.
The output parameter 'data' will be written with the resolved symbol; caller must provide a valid reference.
The output parameter 'ambiguous' will be set to indicate ambiguity; caller must provide a valid reference.
Caller must check the boolean return value: false indicates no suitable overload was found or resolution failed.

functions.name: reshadefx::parser::parser
functions.description: Default constructor for the ReShade FX parser. Initializes internal state (lexer/codegen pointers, token buffers, error storage) to prepare for parsing operations. Use to create a parser instance before calling parse().
requirements: Must be called to construct a parser object before any member functions (e.g., parse, errors) are used.
No arguments; performs initialization only.

functions.name: reshadefx::parser::~parser
functions.description: Destructor for the ReShade FX parser. Cleans up any internal resources owned by the parser instance. After destruction, the object and any references obtained from it (e.g., from errors()) must no longer be used.
requirements: Do not use the parser object or any references returned from it after the destructor has run.
Ensure there are no outstanding operations referencing the parser during destruction (lifetime safety).

functions.name: reshadefx::parser::parse
functions.description: Parses the provided ReShade FX source code and generates code via the given codegen backend. Returns true on successful parse and code generation, false otherwise. On failure, diagnostic messages are available via errors(). Typical usage: construct parser, call parse with the source text and a valid codegen implementation, then query errors() if parse returns false.
requirements: backend must be a valid, non-null pointer to a code generation implementation.
source should contain ReShade FX shader language text; on invalid input, the function returns false and errors() will contain messages.
May modify the provided backend via its interface during code generation; backend must be in a state ready to receive generated code.
Return value must be checked by callers to determine success before relying on generated output.

functions.name: reshadefx::parser::errors
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the accumulated error messages from the most recent or current parsing session. Intended for diagnostics when parse() fails.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the parser object remains alive; do not use after the parser is destroyed.
Callers must not attempt to modify the returned string (const reference).
Meaningful content is typically available after at least one call to parse(); prior to parsing it may be empty.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::preprocessor
functions.description: Constructs a new C-style preprocessor instance that can ingest files/strings, process directives (e.g., #include, #define, #if), and produce preprocessed output and diagnostics. Typical usage: construct, optionally add include paths and macro definitions, then call append_file/append_string and inspect output()/errors().
requirements: Object must be constructed before any member function is used.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::~preprocessor
functions.description: Destroys the preprocessor instance and releases any associated resources (e.g., lexers, caches). After destruction, previously returned references (e.g., from errors() or output()) must no longer be used.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::add_include_path
functions.description: Adds a directory to the search paths used to resolve #include directives. Call before or during parsing to influence how subsequent #include directives are resolved.
requirements: The provided path is intended to be a directory used for include resolution (existence and accessibility are not specified here).

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::add_macro_definition
functions.description: Defines or updates a macro as if by a '#define name definition' directive. Returns true if the macro did not previously exist, false otherwise. Use this to inject function-like or object-like macros (with parameters, variadic flags, etc.).
requirements: 'name' should be a valid macro identifier.
'definition' should describe the macro's replacement_list and, for function-like macros, its parameters and flags.
Call before or during parsing to affect subsequent preprocessing.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::append_file
functions.description: Opens and parses the specified file and appends the preprocessed result to the current output. Returns true on successful parsing, false otherwise. Intended for feeding source files that may contain preprocessor directives.
requirements: 'path' should refer to a readable source file to parse.
Callers should check the boolean return value to detect failures and may inspect errors() for diagnostics.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::append_string
functions.description: Parses the provided source string and appends the preprocessed result to the current output. Optionally supply a path to identify this input in diagnostics. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
requirements: 'source_code' should contain the text to preprocess.
If provided, 'path' is used only for identification/diagnostics.
Callers should check the boolean return value and inspect errors() on failure.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::errors
functions.description: Returns a reference to the accumulated error messages produced during preprocessing. Use after append_file/append_string to retrieve diagnostics.
requirements: The returned reference is tied to the lifetime of the preprocessor instance; do not use it after the object is destroyed.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::output
functions.description: Returns a reference to the current preprocessed output buffer. Use after feeding inputs to obtain the expanded text.
requirements: The returned reference is tied to the lifetime of the preprocessor instance; do not use it after the object is destroyed.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::included_files
functions.description: Retrieves a list of file system paths to all files that were included via #include during preprocessing.
requirements: None beyond having performed preprocessing that may include files.

functions.name: reshadefx::preprocessor::used_macro_definitions
functions.description: Returns a list of macros referenced in #ifdef and #ifndef directives, along with associated information (name and value). Useful for analyzing conditional compilation usage.
requirements: None beyond having performed preprocessing that may have encountered #ifdef/#ifndef directives.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::~codegen
functions.description: Virtual destructor of the SSA code generation back-end interface. Ensures proper cleanup of derived implementations when deleted via a base pointer.
requirements: The object must have been created by a valid implementation of reshadefx::codegen.
Do not use any references returned by member functions after the destructor has run.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::module
functions.description: Returns a reference to the effect_module that describes the generated code (textures, samplers, storages, uniforms, functions, techniques, etc.). Use this to inspect or augment module-level metadata.
requirements: The returned reference becomes invalid once the codegen instance is destroyed.
Caller must not assume thread-safety when accessing the returned module reference.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::finalize_code
functions.description: Finalize and return the generated code for the entire module (all entry points). Intended for back-ends that emit textual code (e.g., GLSL/HLSL).
requirements: Must be called after the IR/code for all functions and entry points has been emitted.
May be called at most once per final output for a given back-end instance; repeated calls may return the same or undefined content depending on implementation (unknown).
If the back-end produces binary artifacts, prefer assemble_code_for_entry_point instead (when applicable).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::assemble_code_for_entry_point
functions.signature: virtual bool assemble_code_for_entry_point(const std::string &entry_point_name, std::string &binary, std::string &assembly, std::string &errors) const
functions.description: Finalize and assemble code for a single specified entry point, producing binary and/or assembly output alongside any errors. Does not assemble other entry points.
requirements: entry_point_name should name a function that was previously defined and made an entry point (exact requirements are implementation-defined; unknown).
binary, assembly, and errors are output parameters and will be written by the implementation; their prior contents may be overwritten.
Call only after all code generation for the target entry point has completed.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_struct
functions.description: Define a new struct type in the module and assign it a new SSA type ID. The provided struct_type is populated/updated and recorded.
requirements: info must describe the struct layout expected by the target back-end (fields, names, etc.).
loc should reference the source location for debugging; it is not required to be non-empty.
Must be called before using the struct type to define variables or function parameters of that type.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_texture
functions.description: Define a new texture binding and assign it a new SSA ID. Records the texture in the module.
requirements: info must describe the texture (dimension, format, binding details) in a way the back-end expects.
Must be called before defining samplers/storages referencing this texture or emitting operations that use it.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_sampler
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id define_sampler(const location &loc, const texture &tex_info, sampler &info)
functions.description: Define a new sampler binding referencing a texture and assign it a new SSA ID. Records the sampler in the module.
requirements: tex_info must reference a previously defined texture.
info must contain sampler state expected by the target back-end.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_storage
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id define_storage(const location &loc, const texture &tex_info, storage &info)
functions.description: Define a new storage binding for a texture and assign it a new SSA ID. Records the storage in the module.
requirements: tex_info must reference a previously defined texture compatible with storage usage.
info must describe the storage access/format as required by the back-end.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_uniform
functions.description: Define a new uniform variable and assign it a new SSA ID. Records the uniform in the module.
requirements: info must describe a valid uniform (type, name, binding layout as applicable).
Must be called before the uniform is referenced in code emission.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_variable
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id define_variable(const location &loc, const type &type, std::string name = std::string(), bool global = false, reshadefx::codegen::id initializer_value = 0)
functions.description: Define a new variable (global or local) with optional name and initializer, returning a new SSA ID for it.
requirements: type must be a valid data type known to the back-end.
If global is true, variable is defined at global scope; otherwise at current function scope (implementation-defined handling; unknown).
If initializer_value is non-zero, it must be an SSA ID of a compatible value.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_function
functions.description: Define a new function with parameters and make it the current function; subsequent emitted code is added to this function. Returns the function's SSA ID.
requirements: info must fully describe the function signature (name, return type, parameters).
Must be paired with a later leave_function() to end emission for this function before starting another (unless the implementation supports nesting; unknown).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_technique
functions.description: Add a new effect technique to the module. Moves the provided technique into module.techniques.
requirements: info is moved-from after the call and must not be used by the caller.
The technique content must be valid for the target runtime (passes, annotations, etc.).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::define_entry_point
functions.description: Mark a function as a shader entry point. Implementations may replace the referenced function with a newly generated unique function object.
requirements: function must reference a function previously defined via define_function.
Caller should be prepared that the function reference may be overwritten to another function object representing the entry point.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_load
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_load(const expression &chain, bool force_new_id = false)
functions.description: Resolve an access chain and emit a load from the addressed l-value, producing an SSA value ID of the loaded data.
requirements: chain must resolve to a readable location.
If force_new_id is true, the implementation must not return an SSA ID that aliases a prior l-value load.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_store
functions.signature: virtual void emit_store(const expression &chain, reshadefx::codegen::id value)
functions.description: Resolve an access chain and emit a store to the addressed l-value using the provided SSA value.
requirements: chain must resolve to a writable location.
value must be an SSA ID of a value compatible with the destination type.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_access_chain
functions.description: Resolve an access chain but do not emit a load; returns an SSA ID representing a pointer/reference to the addressed value. The out-parameter chain_index is set to the depth reached in the chain. Default implementation sets chain_index to the full chain length and falls back to emit_load(chain).
requirements: chain must describe a resolvable access path.
Implementations overriding this should set chain_index to the index up to which the chain was resolved.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_constant
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_constant(const type &type, const constant &data)
functions.description: Create an SSA constant of the specified type from raw constant data and return its SSA ID.
requirements: type must be a valid scalar/vector/matrix/aggregate type supported by the back-end.
data must contain components compatible with 'type' layout and size.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_unary_op
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_unary_op(const location &loc, tokenid op, const type &type, reshadefx::codegen::id val)
functions.description: Emit a built-in unary operation on a value and return the result SSA ID.
requirements: op must be a valid unary operator token for 'type'.
val must be an SSA ID of a value compatible with 'type'.
loc should indicate the source location for debugging (optional).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_binary_op
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_binary_op(const location &loc, tokenid op, const type &res_type, const type &type, reshadefx::codegen::id lhs, reshadefx::codegen::id rhs)
functions.description: Emit a built-in binary operation on two values and return the result SSA ID, allowing a result type distinct from the operand type (e.g., comparisons).
requirements: op must be a valid binary operator token for 'type'.
lhs and rhs must be SSA IDs of values compatible with 'type'.
res_type must be a valid result type for the operator (e.g., boolean for comparisons).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_ternary_op
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_ternary_op(const location &loc, tokenid op, const type &type, reshadefx::codegen::id condition, reshadefx::codegen::id true_value, reshadefx::codegen::id false_value)
functions.description: Emit a built-in ternary operation (e.g., conditional select) and return the result SSA ID.
requirements: op must be a valid ternary operator token for 'type'.
condition, true_value, false_value must be SSA IDs of compatible types expected by the operator.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_call
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_call(const location &loc, reshadefx::codegen::id function, const type &res_type, const std::vector<expression> &args)
functions.description: Emit a function call to a user-defined function and return the result SSA ID.
requirements: function must be an SSA ID referencing a previously defined function.
args must match the callee parameter types and arity.
res_type must match the function return type.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_call_intrinsic
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_call_intrinsic(const location &loc, reshadefx::codegen::id function, const type &res_type, const std::vector<expression> &args)
functions.description: Emit a call to an intrinsic/built-in function and return the result SSA ID.
requirements: function must identify a recognized intrinsic for the back-end.
args must match the intrinsic's expected types and arity.
res_type must be valid for the intrinsic.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_construct
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_construct(const location &loc, const type &type, const std::vector<expression> &args)
functions.description: Emit a type constructor to build a value of the specified type from scalar or sub-aggregate arguments and return the SSA ID of the constructed value.
requirements: type must be constructible from 'args' according to the language rules for the back-end.
args must provide enough components to initialize 'type'.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_if
functions.signature: virtual void emit_if(const location &loc, reshadefx::codegen::id condition_value, reshadefx::codegen::id condition_block, reshadefx::codegen::id true_statement_block, reshadefx::codegen::id false_statement_block, unsigned int flags)
functions.description: Emit a structured branch (if-then-else) with blocks for condition, true, and false paths. Flags control flattening behavior (0 default, 1 flatten, 2 do not flatten).
requirements: condition_value must be an SSA ID of a boolean-like value usable in a branch.
condition_block, true_statement_block, false_statement_block must be valid basic block IDs created by create_block/enter_block.
flags must be one of {0,1,2} as documented.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_phi
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id emit_phi(const location &loc, reshadefx::codegen::id condition_value, reshadefx::codegen::id condition_block, reshadefx::codegen::id true_value, reshadefx::codegen::id true_statement_block, reshadefx::codegen::id false_value, reshadefx::codegen::id false_statement_block, const type &type)
functions.description: Emit a branch with an SSA phi selection of values coming from true/false paths, returning the merged SSA result.
requirements: true_value and false_value must be SSA IDs of values compatible with 'type'.
condition_value must be a boolean-like SSA ID used to select between paths.
All block IDs provided must be valid and correspond to the control-flow structure being emitted.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_loop
functions.signature: virtual void emit_loop(const location &loc, reshadefx::codegen::id condition_value, reshadefx::codegen::id prev_block, reshadefx::codegen::id header_block, reshadefx::codegen::id condition_block, reshadefx::codegen::id loop_block, reshadefx::codegen::id continue_block, unsigned int flags)
functions.description: Emit a structured loop with explicit blocks for header, condition, loop body, and continue paths. Flags control unrolling (0 default, 1 unroll, 2 do not unroll).
requirements: All block IDs must be valid blocks created beforehand.
condition_value must be a boolean-like SSA ID used for loop control.
flags must be one of {0,1,2} as documented.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_switch
functions.signature: virtual void emit_switch(const location &loc, reshadefx::codegen::id selector_value, reshadefx::codegen::id selector_block, reshadefx::codegen::id default_label, reshadefx::codegen::id default_block, const std::vector<reshadefx::codegen::id> &case_literal_and_labels, const std::vector<reshadefx::codegen::id> &case_blocks, unsigned int flags)
functions.description: Emit a structured switch with a selector value, default label/block, and lists of case literals with labels and their corresponding case blocks. Flags control flattening (0 default, 1 flatten, 2 do not flatten).
requirements: selector_value must be an SSA ID of an integer-like value suitable as a switch selector.
selector_block, default_block, and entries in case_blocks must be valid blocks.
case_literal_and_labels must contain pairs [literal,label] as IDs in the order expected by the implementation (exact encoding is implementation-defined; unknown).
flags must be one of {0,1,2}.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::emit_pragma
functions.description: Emit a pragma directive with the given argument into the output stream for the back-end.
requirements: pragma string must be supported/understood by the target back-end; unsupported pragmas may be ignored or cause errors (implementation-defined).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::is_in_block
functions.description: Return true if code is currently being added to a basic block.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::is_in_function
functions.description: Return true if code is currently being added to a function.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::create_block
functions.description: Create a new basic block and return its ID. Default implementation generates a fresh SSA ID via make_id().
requirements: Caller should subsequently use enter_block or set_block to make the block current before emitting instructions into it.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::set_block
functions.description: Overwrite the current block with the given block ID, returning the previous block ID.
requirements: id must be a valid basic block ID previously created.
Must be called while inside a function context (i.e., after define_function).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::enter_block
functions.description: Create (if needed) and make the specified basic block current so subsequent emissions go into it.
requirements: id must be a valid or reserved basic block ID for the current function as expected by the implementation.
Must be called while inside a function context.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::leave_block_and_kill
functions.description: Terminate the current basic block and emit a kill/terminate instruction for the shader invocation. Returns the current block ID.
requirements: Must be called while a current basic block is active.
Semantics of 'kill' depend on shader stage/back-end.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::leave_block_and_return
functions.description: Terminate the current basic block and emit a return (optionally with a value). Returns the current block ID.
requirements: Must be called while a current basic block is active within a function.
If value is non-zero, it must be an SSA ID compatible with the function's return type.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::leave_block_and_switch
functions.description: Diverge control flow from the current block into a switch driven by 'value', providing a default target block.
requirements: value must be an SSA ID suitable for switch selection (integer-like).
default_target must be a valid basic block ID.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::leave_block_and_branch
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id leave_block_and_branch(reshadefx::codegen::id target, unsigned int loop_flow = 0)
functions.description: Diverge control flow and branch unconditionally to 'target'. The optional loop_flow parameter can indicate special loop-related flow (e.g., continue). Returns the current block ID.
requirements: target must be a valid basic block ID.
loop_flow must match implementation-defined values for loop semantics (0 default; other values implementation-defined; unknown).
Must be called while a current basic block is active.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::leave_block_and_branch_conditional
functions.signature: virtual reshadefx::codegen::id leave_block_and_branch_conditional(reshadefx::codegen::id condition, reshadefx::codegen::id true_target, reshadefx::codegen::id false_target)
functions.description: Diverge control flow and branch to either 'true_target' or 'false_target' based on 'condition'. Returns the current block ID.
requirements: condition must be a boolean-like SSA ID.
true_target and false_target must be valid basic block IDs.
Must be called while a current basic block is active.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::leave_function
functions.description: Leave the current function. Any subsequent code emission happens in global scope until another define_function call.
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching define_function that made a function current.
No basic blocks should remain unterminated if required by the back-end (implementation-specific; unknown).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::optimize_bindings
functions.description: Compute sampler and storage bindings to minimize binding space usage per entry point.
requirements: Should be called after all textures/samplers/storages and entry points have been defined.
Effects of multiple calls are implementation-defined (unknown).

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::get_struct
functions.description: Look up and return a reference to an existing struct_type by its SSA ID.
requirements: id must correspond to a previously defined struct via define_struct.
Returned reference is valid as long as the codegen instance lives.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::get_texture
functions.description: Look up and return a reference to an existing texture by its SSA ID.
requirements: id must correspond to a previously defined texture via define_texture.
Returned reference remains valid while the module stores it and the codegen instance exists.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::get_sampler
functions.description: Look up and return a reference to an existing sampler by its SSA ID.
requirements: id must correspond to a previously defined sampler via define_sampler.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::get_storage
functions.description: Look up and return a reference to an existing storage binding by its SSA ID.
requirements: id must correspond to a previously defined storage via define_storage.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::get_function
functions.description: Look up and return a reference to a function definition by its SSA ID.
requirements: id must correspond to a previously defined function via define_function.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::find_function
functions.description: Find a function by its unique_name and return a mutable pointer, or nullptr if not found.
requirements: unique_name must match the function's unique_name property to succeed.

functions.name: reshadefx::codegen::make_id
functions.description: Generate and return a fresh SSA ID by incrementing the internal counter.
requirements: IDs are unique per codegen instance; caller must not assume stability across instances.

functions.name: reshadefx::create_codegen_glsl
functions.signature: codegen *create_codegen_glsl(bool vulkan_semantics, bool debug_info, bool uniforms_to_spec_constants, bool enable_16bit_types = false, bool flip_vert_y = false)
functions.description: Factory function to create a GLSL back-end implementation of codegen. Supports OpenGL or Vulkan GLSL semantics and optional 16-bit types and vertex Y flip.
requirements: Caller owns the returned pointer and is responsible for deleting it via the appropriate destructor (delete through base pointer).
vulkan_semantics selects SPIR-V/Vulkan-style GLSL if true, otherwise OpenGL-style.
If enable_16bit_types is true, minimum-precision types use real 16-bit types.

functions.name: reshadefx::create_codegen_hlsl
functions.signature: codegen *create_codegen_hlsl(unsigned int shader_model, bool debug_info, bool uniforms_to_spec_constants)
functions.description: Factory function to create an HLSL text back-end implementation of codegen for a given shader model.
requirements: Caller owns the returned pointer and must delete it via the base destructor.
shader_model must be a supported HLSL shader model value (e.g., 30, 41, 50, 60, ...).

functions.name: reshadefx::create_codegen_dxbc
functions.signature: codegen *create_codegen_dxbc(unsigned int shader_model, bool debug_info, bool uniforms_to_spec_constants, int optimization_level)
functions.description: Factory function to create a DXBC back-end implementation of codegen with a given shader model and optimization level.
requirements: Caller owns the returned pointer and must delete it via the base destructor.
shader_model must be a supported DXBC-level shader model.
optimization_level must be within the implementation-supported range (exact range unknown).

functions.name: reshadefx::create_codegen_dxil
functions.signature: codegen *create_codegen_dxil(unsigned int shader_model, bool debug_info, bool uniforms_to_spec_constants, int optimization_level)

data_types.description: A free-form source text buffer following C-like lexical conventions (identifiers, operators, punctuation, comments, preprocessor directives). May be shader-style (ReShade FX/HLSL/GLSL-like). Used as input to lexers/parsers/preprocessors.

A sanitized identifier token suitable for programming languages like C/C++/shader languages. Begins with a letter or underscore, followed by letters, digits, or underscores. Used for namespaces, symbols, and function names.

A filesystem path string (absolute or relative). May include directories and filenames. Used to locate files or represent source locations; the content pointed to by the path may be arbitrary fuzz data.
An unconstrained byte string used as general text payload (e.g., macro replacement list, string literal contents). No specific encoding or format required.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target data type: C-like source code for ReShade FX/HLSL-like lexer/parser/preprocessor.
# Goal: Generate valid, interesting source that exercises tokens, comments, directives,
# literals, identifiers, keywords, types, functions, techniques/passes, and various punctuation.
# The fuzzer stubs will feed this buffer to FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# We therefore craft a single bytes payload that contains multiple segments separated by newlines,
# each segment being valid C-like code or preprocessor lines, within 4096 bytes.

KW_TYPES = [
    "void","bool","int","uint","float","double",
    "min16int","min16uint","min16float",
    "bool2","bool3","bool4","int2","int3","int4","uint2","uint3","uint4",
    "float2","float3","float4","float2x2","float3x3","float4x4",
]

KW_STORAGE = ["extern","static","uniform","volatile","precise","groupshared","const"]
KW_INOUT = ["in","out","inout"]
KW_FLOW = ["if","else","for","while","do","switch","case","default","break","continue","return","discard"]
KW_NS = ["namespace"]
KW_TECH = ["technique","pass"]

OPS_SINGLE = list("!#$%&()*,+-./:;<>?@[]\\]^{}|~=")
OPS_MULTI = [
    "!=", "%=", "&&", "&=", "*=", "++", "+=", "--", "-=", "->", "...", "/=", "::",
    "<<=", "<<", "<=", "==", ">>=", ">>", ">=", "^=", "|=", "||"
]

# Common identifiers and semantics
ID_BASE = [
    "main","VS","PS","CS","MyFunc","DoThing","Update","Compute","Foo","Bar","Baz",
    "g_Time","g_Frame","g_Toggle","Tex","Tex2","Tex3","Samp","Store","Ubo","ubo0",
]
SEMANTICS = ["POSITION","NORMAL","TEXCOORD0","TEXCOORD1","COLOR","SV_Target","SV_Position"]

TEXTURE_OBJS = [
    ("texture1D", "texture1d"), ("texture2D", "texture2d"), ("texture3D", "texture3d")
]

SAMPLER_KINDS = [
    ("sampler1D", "sampler1d_float"), ("sampler2D", "sampler2d_float"), ("sampler3D", "sampler3d_float")
]

FORMATS = [
    "r8","r16f","r16","r32f","r32u","r32i","rg8","rg16f","rg16","rg32f","rgba8","rgba16f","rgba16",
    "rgba32f","rgba32u","rgba32i","rgb10a2","rg11b10f"
]

FILTERS = [
    "min_mag_mip_point","min_mag_point_mip_linear","min_point_mag_linear_mip_point","min_point_mag_mip_linear",
    "min_linear_mag_mip_point","min_linear_mag_point_mip_linear","min_mag_linear_mip_point","min_mag_mip_linear","anisotropic"
]

ADDRESS = ["wrap","mirror","clamp","border"]

def rchoice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def rand_ident(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 10)))
    return start + rest

def rand_int_lit(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    bases = [10, 16]
    b = rng.choice(bases)
    if b == 16:
        val = hex(rng.randrange(0, 1<<16))
    else:
        val = str(rng.randrange(0, 1<<16))
    suffix = rng.choice(["", "u", "U"])
    return val + suffix

def rand_float_lit(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Simple decimal or scientific
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = f"{rng.uniform(-1000,1000):.6f}"
    else:
        mant = rng.uniform(0.1, 1000.0)
        exp = rng.randint(-10, 10)
        s = f"{mant:.6e}"
        # normalize exponent sign/width
        if "e" in s:
            base, _e = s.split("e")
            s = f"{base}e{exp:+d}"
    return s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.') if '.' in s else s

def rand_string_lit(rng: random.Random, maxlen: int = 24) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(0, maxlen)
    # include escape sequences to exercise escape_string_literals
    chars = []
    for _ in range(length):
        ch = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:/\\\"'!@#$%^&*()[]{}.,<>?|")
        if ch == '"':
            chars.append('\\"')
        elif ch == '\\':
            chars.append('\\\\')
        elif ch == '\n' or (rng.random() < 0.02):
            chars.append('\\n')
        else:
            chars.append(ch)
    return '"' + ''.join(chars) + '"'

def gen_comment_block(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # mix single-line and multi-line
    parts = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append("// " + rand_ident(rng) + " " + rand_string_lit(rng, 12))
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        inner = "*".join(rand_ident(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(1,4)))
        parts.append("/* " + inner + " */")
    return "\n".join(parts) + "\n"

def gen_pp_block(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    # Some defines
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        name = rand_ident(rng).upper()
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"#define {name} {rng.randint(0, 5)}")
        else:
            # function-like macro
            pcount = rng.randint(0, 2)
            params = ",".join(rand_ident(rng) for _ in range(pcount))
            body = rchoice(rng, [rand_ident(rng), rand_int_lit(rng), rand_float_lit(rng)])
            lines.append(f"#define {name}({params}) {body}")
    # Conditional
    used = rand_ident(rng).upper()
    lines.append(f"#ifdef {used}")
    lines.append("#warning inside ifdef")
    lines.append("#else")
    lines.append("#pragma message: else-branch")
    lines.append("#endif")
    # include with pseudo path; fuzzer maps FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME extern, but a literal path is fine too
    lines.append(f"#include \"{rand_ident(rng)}.fxh\"")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def gen_struct(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    name = rand_ident(rng)
    members = []
    for i in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        t = rchoice(rng, KW_TYPES)
        mname = rand_ident(rng)
        sem = rchoice(rng, SEMANTICS)
        members.append(f"    {t} {mname} : {sem};")
    return "struct " + name + " {\n" + "\n".join(members) + "\n};\n"

def gen_texture_and_sampler(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    # texture resource (ReShade FX style)
    tname = rand_ident(rng)
    width = rng.randint(1, 1024)
    height = rng.randint(1, 1024)
    depth = rng.randint(1, 32)
    fmt = rchoice(rng, FORMATS)
    lines.append(f"texture {tname} < source = {rand_string_lit(rng, 14)}, width = {width}, height = {height}, depth = {depth}, format = {fmt} > {{}};")
    # sampler referencing texture
    sname = rand_ident(rng)
    filt = rchoice(rng, FILTERS)
    au, av, aw = rchoice(rng, ADDRESS), rchoice(rng, ADDRESS), rchoice(rng, ADDRESS)
    lines.append(f"sampler {sname} : register(s{rng.randint(0,7)}) {{ Texture = {tname}; Filter = {filt}; AddressU = {au}; AddressV = {av}; AddressW = {aw}; }}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def gen_uniforms(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        t = rchoice(rng, KW_TYPES)
        name = rand_ident(rng)
        init = None
        if t in ("int","uint","bool","min16int","min16uint"):
            init = rand_int_lit(rng)
        elif t in ("float","double","min16float"):
            init = rand_float_lit(rng)
        elif t == "string":
            init = rand_string_lit(rng, 10)
        ann = f"< ui_label = {rand_string_lit(rng,8)} >" if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""
        if init is not None and rng.random() < 0.7:
            lines.append(f"uniform {t} {name} {ann} = {init};")
        else:
            lines.append(f"uniform {t} {name} {ann};")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def gen_function(rng: random.Random, stage: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    # stage in {vertex, pixel, compute}
    ret = rchoice(rng, ["void","float4","int","bool"]) if stage != "compute" else "void"
    fname = rand_ident(rng)
    params = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        t = rchoice(rng, KW_TYPES)
        q = rng.choice(["", rchoice(rng, KW_INOUT)+" "])
        params.append(f"{q}{t} {rand_ident(rng)}")
    param_str = ", ".join(params)
    body = []
    # local variables
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        t = rchoice(rng, KW_TYPES)
        name = rand_ident(rng)
        if t in ("int","uint","bool","min16int","min16uint"):
            body.append(f"    {t} {name} = {rand_int_lit(rng)};")
        elif t in ("float","double","min16float","float2","float3","float4"):
            body.append(f"    {t} {name} = {rand_float_lit(rng)};")
        else:
            body.append(f"    {t} {name};")
    # control flow
    body.append(f"    if ({rng.choice(['true','false'])}) {{ }} else {{ }}")
    body.append(f"    for (int i = 0; i < {rng.randint(1,4)}; ++i) {{ continue; }}")
    body.append(f"    while ({rng.choice(['true','false'])}) break;")
    if ret == "void":
        body.append("    return;")
    elif ret == "float4":
        body.append("    return float4(0.0, 1.0, 0.5, 1.0);")
    elif ret == "int":
        body.append("    return 0;")
    else:
        body.append("    return false;")
    func = f"{ret} {fname}({param_str}) {{\n" + "\n".join(body) + "\n}\n"
    return func, fname

def gen_technique(rng: random.Random, vs: str, ps: str) -> str:
    tech_name = rand_ident(rng)
    passes = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        pname = rand_ident(rng)
        # random blend/stencil bits within valid names
        blend_enable = rng.choice(["true","false"])
        sRGB = rng.choice(["true","false"])
        passes.append(
            "    pass " + pname + " {\n"
            + (f"        VertexShader = {vs};\n" if vs else "")
            + (f"        PixelShader = {ps};\n" if ps else "")
            + f"        BlendEnable = {blend_enable};\n"
            + f"        SRGBWriteEnable = {sRGB};\n"
            + "    }"
        )
    return "technique " + tech_name + " {\n" + "\n".join(passes) + "\n}\n"

def gen_filename_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Provide a plausible filename path that the harness may use for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME mapping
    # Keep it within the buffer as a comment for the preprocessor stub to potentially pick up
    parts = [rand_ident(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(1,3))]
    fname = rand_ident(rng) + rng.choice([".fx",".fxh",".hlsl",".glsl"])
    return "/".join(parts + [fname])

def assemble_source(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> str:
    sections = []
    # location directive like lines to exercise line directives and locations
    sections.append(gen_comment_block(rng))
    sections.append(gen_pp_block(rng))
    # namespace and struct
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        sections.append(f"namespace {rand_ident(rng)} {{}}\n")
    sections.append(gen_struct(rng))
    # textures/samplers and uniforms
    sections.append(gen_texture_and_sampler(rng))
    sections.append(gen_uniforms(rng))
    # functions
    f_vs, name_vs = gen_function(rng, "vertex")
    f_ps, name_ps = gen_function(rng, "pixel")
    sections.append(f_vs)
    sections.append(f_ps)
    # technique binding
    sections.append(gen_technique(rng, name_vs, name_ps))
    # sprinkle operators and literals line to exercise tokenization
    multi_k = min(5, len(OPS_MULTI))
    multi_pick = rng.sample(OPS_MULTI, k=multi_k)
    single_k = min(10, len(OPS_SINGLE))
    single_pick = rng.sample(OPS_SINGLE, k=single_k)
    ops_line = " ".join(multi_pick) + " " + " ".join(single_pick)
    lit_line = f"{rand_int_lit(rng)} {rand_float_lit(rng)} {rand_string_lit(rng, 16)} true false"
    sections.append("// operators\n" + ops_line + "\n")
    sections.append("// literals\n" + lit_line + "\n")
    # embed a plausible filename as a comment for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME users to see
    sections.append("// file: " + gen_filename_like(rng) + "\n")

    src = "\n".join(sections)
    if len(src) > budget:
        src = src[:budget]
    return src


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Budget: up to 2048 preferred for lexer stub, but global limit is 4096.
    budget = rng.randint(512, 2048)
    source = assemble_source(rng, budget)
    # Ensure non-empty and newline-terminated for lexing behavior on end_of_line
    if not source.endswith("\n"):
        source += "\n"
    return source.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzer stubs that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR for
# identifiers, macro names, replacement lists, and source filenames/contents,
# as well as integers for locations/types. We therefore return a bytes buffer
# that contains a sequence of ASCII tokens and numbers which the harness can
# slice to satisfy FUZZ_PARAM_* requests. The buffer is designed to contain:
# - Many valid identifiers (for namespaces, symbols, function names, params)
# - Macro replacement texts that include typical C-like tokens
# - Mixed numeric literals to feed uint32_t and unsigned int uses
# - Source-like content lines to act as plausible file/string inputs
# The data stays within 4096 bytes.

IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + string.digits

C_TOKENS = [
    "+", "-", "*", "/", "%", "&", "|", "^", "~",
    "=", "==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=",
    "&&", "||", "!", "++", "--",
    ",", ";", ":", "::", ".", "->",
    "(", ")", "[", "]", "{", "}",
]

KEYWORDS = [
    "namespace", "struct", "technique", "pass", "for", "while", "if", "else",
    "switch", "case", "default", "break", "continue", "return", "discard",
    "extern", "static", "uniform", "volatile", "const", "in", "out", "inout",
    "bool", "int", "uint", "float", "double", "string",
]

# Common identifier stems to increase chance of resolution/linkage across calls
STEMS = [
    "ns", "sym", "func", "f", "g", "h", "macro", "param", "Type", "MyStruct",
    "Texture", "Sampler", "Storage", "Pass", "Technique",
]


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        s += rng.choice(IDENT_CONT)
    return s


def _rand_identifier_from_stems(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix predefined stems with random suffixes to get stable but varied names
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        stem = rng.choice(STEMS)
        # Append alnum/underscore suffix
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            stem += rng.choice(["_", "", "__"]) + _rand_ident(rng, 1, 8)
        return stem
    return _rand_ident(rng, 1, 16)


def _rand_uint(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Prefer small numbers but occasionally large ones
    if rng.random() < 0.85:
        return rng.randrange(0, 1000)
    return rng.getrandbits(32)


def _rand_rows_cols(rng: random.Random) -> (int, int):
    # 1..4 as used by the fuzzer stub
    return rng.randint(1, 4), rng.randint(1, 4)


def _rand_string_literal(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    # Produce a plausible string literal body
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./"
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s


def _make_macro_def(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a function-like or object-like macro definition text
    name = _rand_identifier_from_stems(rng)
    is_func = rng.random() < 0.6
    params: List[str] = []
    if is_func:
        pcount = rng.randint(0, 3)
        for i in range(pcount):
            params.append(_rand_identifier_from_stems(rng))
    repl_parts: List[str] = []
    # Build replacement with mixture of identifiers, numbers, and tokens
    part_count = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(part_count):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.4:
            repl_parts.append(_rand_identifier_from_stems(rng))
        elif choice < 0.7:
            repl_parts.append(str(_rand_uint(rng) % 1024))
        else:
            repl_parts.append(rng.choice(C_TOKENS))
    replacement = ' '.join(repl_parts)
    if is_func:
        return f"#define {name}({', '.join(params)}) {replacement}"
    else:
        return f"#define {name} {replacement}"


def _make_source_snippet(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a few lines resembling reshadefx language input for lexer/pp
    lines: List[str] = []
    # Some includes and pragmas
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        inc_name = _rand_identifier_from_stems(rng) + ".fxh"
        lines.append(f"#include \"{inc_name}\"")
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        lines.append("#pragma message(\"hello\")")
    # A couple of macro definitions
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        lines.append(_make_macro_def(rng))
    # A namespace and symbol-looking declarations
    ns = _rand_identifier_from_stems(rng)
    lines.append(f"namespace {ns} {{")
    # Variables/uniform-like lines
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        t = rng.choice(["int", "uint", "float", "bool"]) \
            + (rng.choice(["", "2", "3", "4"]) if rng.random() < 0.5 else "")
        name = _rand_identifier_from_stems(rng)
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            lines.append(f"static {t} {name} = {rng.randint(0, 10)};")
        else:
            lines.append(f"extern {t} {name};")
    # A function/prototype-like
    ret = rng.choice(["void", "float", "int", "bool"]) \
        + (rng.choice(["", "2", "3", "4"]) if rng.random() < 0.3 else "")
    fname = _rand_identifier_from_stems(rng)
    # Parameters
    pcount = rng.randint(0, 3)
    params = []
    for i in range(pcount):
        pt = rng.choice(["float", "int", "uint", "bool"]) \
            + (rng.choice(["", "2", "3", "4"]) if rng.random() < 0.3 else "")
        params.append(f"{pt} {_rand_identifier_from_stems(rng)}")
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        lines.append(f"{ret} {fname}({', '.join(params)}) {{ return; }}")
    else:
        lines.append(f"{ret} {fname}({', '.join(params)});")
    lines.append("}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _emit_uint_block(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> str:
    # Emit a block of decimal uints separated by spaces/newlines
    nums = []
    for _ in range(count):
        nums.append(str(_rand_uint(rng)))
    # mix separators
    sep = rng.choice([" ", "\n", "\t"]) 
    return sep.join(nums)


def _build_buffer(rng: random.Random, target_size: int = 2048) -> bytes:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Header marker to help delimitation in consumers that scan
    parts.append("/* reshadefx seed block */\n")

    # A sequence of sanitized identifiers for names/namespaces/symbols
    idents = [
        _rand_identifier_from_stems(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 20))
    ]
    parts.append("\n".join(idents) + "\n\n")

    # Several macro definitions and replacement texts
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        parts.append(_make_macro_def(rng) + "\n")
    parts.append("\n")

    # Source-like snippets for lexer/preprocessor consumption
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        parts.append(_make_source_snippet(rng) + "\n\n")

    # A pool of numbers for line/column/base/type parameters
    parts.append(_emit_uint_block(rng, rng.randint(20, 60)) + "\n\n")

    # Additional lines of plausible identifiers and keywords mixed
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        line = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                line.append(rng.choice(KEYWORDS))
            elif rng.random() < 0.6:
                line.append(_rand_identifier_from_stems(rng))
            else:
                line.append(rng.choice(C_TOKENS))
        parts.append(" ".join(line) + "\n")

    # String-literal-like content that may be used as FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        s = _rand_string_literal(rng, max_len=48)
        parts.append(s + "\n")

    blob = ("".join(parts)).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    # Trim to limit
    return blob[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Vary internal seed to yield differing results for the same external seed
    # across multiple calls in a run by mixing with a random nonce derived from seed
    # but still deterministic for given seed.
    rng.jumpahead(seed % (10**6)) if hasattr(rng, 'jumpahead') else rng.random()
    return _build_buffer(rng)
